chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abu Shayba, from Al-Zuhri, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The worst servant is a servant who has two faces and two tongues, flattering his brother when present and devouring him when absent. If he is given (a bounty), he envies him, and if he is afflicted, he abandons him.

key_terms.ذَوَاتِ اللِّسَانَيْنِ: Two-tongued (speaking differently in presence and absence)

ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of the worst servant according to Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) identifies the 'worst servant' as one exhibiting *tadlis* (duplicity), characterized by a disconnect between public praise and private backbiting, as well as conditional loyalty that shifts from envy in prosperity to abandonment in hardship. This description aligns with the Quranic critique of the *munafiqun* (hypocrites) who lack a firm spiritual foundation, serving as a practical guide for Shia believers to cultivate consistency between their inner intentions (*niyyah*) and outward actions (*amal*).
